title: Mountain Fresh Plus tomato: Characteristics
metaDescription: Mountain Fresh Plus tomato is an F1 hybrid tomato variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Mountain Fresh Plus tomato is an F1 hybrid tomato variety, also sold or known as Mountain Fresh Plus F1 or Mountain Fresh. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical.

heroImage.alt: Young tomato plants on silver plastic mulch beds with bamboo stakes in San Ildefonso, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Mountain Fresh Plus tomato is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Mountain Fresh Plus F1 or Mountain Fresh, this is the same tomato. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [tomato variety finder](/crop-varieties/tomato), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 80 to 85 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Large, firm, semi oblate (flattish round), 180 to 200 g, ripens evenly.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: allied Botanical's large fruited tomato for dry season planting up to the highlands, the only evidence found is the seller's own pages. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual tomato on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Mountain Fresh Plus tomato

Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

items.q: Is Mountain Fresh Plus F1 the same as Mountain Fresh Plus?
items.a: Yes. Mountain Fresh Plus F1 is another name for Mountain Fresh Plus. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mountain Fresh Plus?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
